neurological_exam.additional: CRITICAL: Hashimoto's encephalopathy (HE) is a rare but REAL encephalopathy associated with anti-thyroid antibodies. It presents with cognitive symptoms, seizures, tremor, and ataxia. It is STEROID-RESPONSIVE. In a patient with Hashimoto's, encephalopathy, cognitive changes, and cerebellar-like signs — Hashimoto's encephalopathy MUST be excluded before FND diagnosis. Anti-TPO antibodies are the key test.

patient.chief_complaint: Confusion, tremor, and bilateral leg weakness — 2 weeks progressive
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. O is a 48-year-old accountant with Hashimoto's thyroiditis and depression who presents with 2-week progressive cognitive confusion, tremor, and bilateral leg weakness. She has been working extreme hours during tax season (14 hours/day for 6 weeks). Her symptoms include brain fog, word-finding difficulty, bilateral hand tremor, and progressive difficulty walking. She also reports multiple brief staring episodes (3-4 per week) lasting 10-20 seconds each. Her levothyroxine has been stable for 2 years with last TSH normal 8 months ago. She has a family history of autoimmune thyroid disease. She also has OSA and has not been using her CPAP consistently due to late nights, which has worsened sleep quality. The diagnostic complexity: (1) Hashimoto's encephalopathy is a real steroid-responsive encephalopathy that presents with cognitive decline, tremor, seizures — it MUST be excluded; (2) Sleep deprivation and OSA can cause cognitive symptoms and tremor; (3) FND is possible given psychosocial stressor. This is the most diagnostically complex FND case because a treatable organic encephalopathy (Hashimoto's) must be excluded, and the treatment (steroids) vs FND treatment are completely different.

additional_observations: No cortical or white matter signal changes that would suggest Hashimoto's encephalopathy (HE can produce subtle T2 signal changes in white matter)

results.title: Hashimoto encephalopathy: clinical and neurophysiological features
Steroid-responsive encephalopathy associated with autoimmune thyroiditis (SREAT): clinical characteristics and outcomes

output.summary: Hashimoto's encephalopathy (HE), also known as steroid-responsive encephalopathy associated with autoimmune thyroiditis (SREAT), is characterised by cognitive decline, tremor, seizures or myoclonus, and psychiatric features in association with elevated anti-thyroid antibodies, typically anti-TPO >1000 IU/mL. Thyroid function may be normal, hypothyroid, or hyperthyroid. CSF frequently shows mild pleocytosis and elevated protein. EEG typically demonstrates generalised slowing. Case series report substantial improvement with corticosteroid therapy in confirmed cases. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hashimoto's encephalopathy (SREAT) — steroid-responsive autoimmune encephalopathy, with undertreated hypothyroidism. FND was initially suspected but is not the correct diagnosis.

differential.key_features: ABNORMAL EEG with generalized slowing and triphasic-like discharges — FND produces completely normal EEG; encephalopathic EEG cannot be attributed to FND; CSF shows pleocytosis and oligoclonal bands — FND has normal CSF

TSH 4.8 (undertreated) — hypothyroidism contributes to cognitive symptoms and EEG slowing; however, the degree of encephalopathy, very high anti-TPO (2840 IU/mL), CSF pleocytosis, and dramatic steroid response all suggest primary Hashimoto's encephalopathy rather than simple hypothyroidism
Anti-NMDAR and anti-LGI1 antibodies not tested here but clinical context (Hashimoto's, elevated anti-TPO) strongly favors HE; anti-TPO positive in CSF is diagnostic of HE

differential.diagnosis: Sleep deprivation encephalopathy from OSA/CPAP non-compliance
differential.key_features: CPAP suboptimal use contributes to cognitive impairment but cannot explain CSF pleocytosis, oligoclonal bands, or marked anti-TPO elevation; steroid response confirms autoimmune etiology

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Normal MRI — does not exclude Hashimoto's encephalopathy

optimal_actions.action: EEG — CRITICAL: encephalopathic slowing confirms organic (not FND) process
optimal_actions.expected_finding: ABNORMAL — generalized theta slowing and triphasic-like discharges: cannot be FND

optimal_actions.action: Thyroid panel and anti-TPO/anti-TG antibodies — Hashimoto's encephalopathy exclusion
CSF for HE confirmation — protein, cells, oligoclonal bands, anti-TPO
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Mild pleocytosis, elevated protein, oligoclonal bands, positive CSF anti-TPO

optimal_actions.action: IV methylprednisolone — steroid trial for Hashimoto's encephalopathy

critical_actions: EEG is the KEY discriminator — FND = normal EEG; Hashimoto's encephalopathy = encephalopathic EEG changes
Anti-TPO antibodies mandatory in Hashimoto's patient with encephalopathy
IV methylprednisolone is potentially curative — urgent administration once diagnosis confirmed
contraindicated_actions: Diagnosing FND with an abnormal EEG — FND NEVER produces encephalopathic EEG changes; abnormal EEG mandates organic encephalopathy workup
Withholding steroids if Hashimoto's encephalopathy is confirmed — this is a potentially reversible encephalopathy
key_reasoning_points: FND CANNOT produce encephalopathic EEG changes — generalized slowing and triphasic-like discharges mandate an organic encephalopathy workup before any FND diagnosis
Anti-TPO antibodies >1000 IU/mL in a patient with encephalopathy, EEG slowing, and cognitive decline is HASHIMOTO'S ENCEPHALOPATHY (SREAT) until proven otherwise
CSF anti-TPO positive confirms intrathecal antibody synthesis — this is not just a systemic autoimmune response

This case is a critical teaching example of why organic encephalopathy must be excluded before FND diagnosis — the steroid-responsive encephalopathy would have been missed if FND was diagnosed based on psychosocial stressors alone

red_herrings.data_point: Extreme work stress (14-hour days), sleep deprivation, CPAP non-compliance
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute all symptoms to stress and sleep deprivation (functional/psychosocial), leading to FND diagnosis without thorough organic workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Psychosocial stress is present but EEG is ABNORMAL — FND cannot explain encephalopathic EEG; anti-TPO 2840 and CSF pleocytosis confirm Hashimoto's encephalopathy

red_herrings.data_point: Positive Hoover sign and give-way weakness on exam
red_herrings.intended_effect: Confirm FND diagnosis based on positive functional signs and stop organic workup
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Positive functional signs can occur in Hashimoto's encephalopathy due to diffuse cortical dysfunction affecting voluntary motor output — organic encephalopathy CAN produce some functional-appearing signs; the KEY is the abnormal EEG which cannot be attributed to FND

metadata.notes: Diagnostic puzzle — Hashimoto's encephalopathy (SREAT), NOT FND. Abnormal EEG and anti-TPO >1000 are the keys. This case teaches that FND cannot be diagnosed when EEG shows encephalopathic changes.
